title: FARDC Retakes Four Uvira Highlands Villages, Discovers Mass Grave at Masango
detail: FARDC's Sukola 2 South-South Kivu sector announced Sept 1 that a joint offensive with Burundian troops (FDNB) and Wazalendo militias against the RDF/M23-Twirwaneho/Red Tabara coalition had retaken Malimba, Masango, Ruhua (Ruhuha) and Rubarati in the Hauts-Plateaux (highlands) of Uvira territory, South Kivu, with remnants retreating toward Kashongo and Magunda. Spokesman Sub-Lt. Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji said 15 rebels were killed and 6 surrendered in the Uvira sector, plus 8 killed and 5 surrendered in a parallel Fizi-highlands push that retook Kamimbi, Nagishashu and Irumba — 23 killed and 11 surrendered combined, with several weapons recovered. FARDC said it discovered a mass grave at Masango containing the remains of civilians allegedly killed during the area's occupation by Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and Rwanda-backed M23 forces; the claim has not been independently verified. The gains follow days of fighting across Malimba, Rubarati and Ruhuha reported from Aug 31.

media.caption: FARDC forces in the Hauts-Plateaux of Uvira after retaking Malimba, Masango, Ruhua and Rubarati, Sept 1, 2026

confidenceReason: Casualty and territorial-gain figures are FARDC's own military claims, reported consistently by two independent North/South Kivu outlets; the mass-grave allegation has not been independently verified by MONUSCO or a neutral body.

title: APDEF: ADF Kill 43 Civilians Across 15 Mambasa-Area Villages in Six-Day Campaign
detail: Local monitoring group APDEF Mambasa reported that ADF attacks between Aug 27 and Sept 1 killed at least 43 civilians, burned 53 houses and looted property across 15 localities in Mambasa territory and neighboring Irumu territory, Ituri — Biamu, Mabakuha, Amani, Mahili, Pangite, Lelesi, Kalongo, Bumaere, Kabadjene, Ndakolo, Epululase, Tentera, Kakule, Malimba and Sukisa in Mambasa, plus Bandikafu, Bamande and Bandeseibo in Irumu. The tally encompasses and expands on the Aug 28-29 twin attacks on Mabakuha and Amani villages already logged in this tracker (previously reported at ~21 killed), which APDEF's wider six-day count folds into a larger campaign toll. APDEF said several bodies remained unburied and multiple residents were missing, with no official FARDC or government statement recorded as of Sept 2, and warned that suspected attackers were still moving through the area, disrupting the planned Sept 1 school reopening.

media.caption: Ituri civil society reports 43 civilians killed across 15 Mambasa-area villages in ADF attacks, Aug 27-Sept 1, 2026

confidenceReason: The cumulative toll is a local civil society (APDEF Mambasa) tally corroborated by an independent AllAfrica report; no FARDC or MONUSCO confirmation had been issued, and the count overlaps partially with a previously reported sub-incident at Amani and Mabakuha.

title: Tshisekedi Meets Netanyahu and Herzog in Jerusalem, Reaffirms DRC Sovereignty
detail: President Félix Tshisekedi held talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Isaac Herzog in Jerusalem on Sept 1, days after launching DRC's national dialogue. Tshisekedi told his hosts that sovereignty and territorial integrity are "neither abstract nor negotiable" for the DRC, grounding the position in the UN Charter amid the more-than-three-year AFC/M23 occupation of parts of North and South Kivu that Kinshasa says is backed by Rwanda; the implementation of the DRC-Rwanda peace agreement was also discussed. The two sides agreed to deepen cooperation on agriculture and food security, water, health, technology, security and training, and investment, building on Herzog's November 2025 visit to Kinshasa that marked Israel's return to the DRC after 40 years without formal ties.

media.caption: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu welcomes DRC President Félix Tshisekedi in Jerusalem, Sept 1, 2026

confidenceReason: The meeting, its participants and general themes are corroborated by an independent DRC outlet and Israeli wire coverage; exact meeting sequencing (PM's Office vs. President's Residence) varies slightly across reports.
